Department of Radiology
UMCG (Groningen)
Date: 06 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 19.0 ng/mL, prior biopsy Gleason 4+4, PI-RADS 5
FINDINGS: Prostate volume measures 51.0 mL. A dominant lesion is identified in the peripheral zone at the right apex, measuring approximately 18 x 15 x 12 mm. The lesion demonstrates marked restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) with corresponding low ADC values, and shows early and intense enhancement on DCE. T2-weighted images reveal a hypointense focus disrupting the peripheral zone architecture. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or distant metastases are seen.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right apical peripheral zone. Prostate volume 51.0 mL, PSA density 0.37 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.88825184.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 4.2 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was normal. Ultrasound showed a prostate volume of 48 mL. PSA was repeated in 3 months. Referred to urology for further evaluation.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1: Tissue samples obtained from the prostate demonstrate a Gleason score of 4+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. The architectural patterns include glabrous glands, cribriform areas, and strands of abortive tubules. A cribriform pattern is present as a high-risk feature. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apex right.

Summary: The histological trajectory across the single documented timepoint shows ISUP grade group 4 disease with cribriform architecture in the right apical peripheral zone.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
